questions.topic: Freshness SLAs and Lag Metrics for Ingestion and Index Builds
questions.question: What is freshness in a data backbone?
options: The size of the newest index generation on disk
The time from a source change to visibility in queries
The number of documents the parser handles per hour
The share of answer-cache entries that are still valid

questions.topic: Freshness SLAs and Lag Metrics for Ingestion and Index Builds
questions.question: How does a stage compute its lag?
options: Rows written per second against the target table
Cache misses per minute over the serving window
Disk usage growth measured since the last build
Now minus the newest source timestamp processed

questions.topic: Freshness SLAs and Lag Metrics for Ingestion and Index Builds
questions.question: Lag doubles every hour though the SLA has not yet been breached. Why alert anyway?
options: A growing lag means the consumer trails the producer
Watermarks are discarded once they are an hour old
Freshness SLAs are only evaluated at midnight daily
The index compacts hourly and resets the lag counter

questions.topic: Freshness SLAs and Lag Metrics for Ingestion and Index Builds
questions.question: A full index rebuild takes six hours. What is wrong with the index at publish time?
options: It is missing the term dictionary the postings need
It is already six hours stale the moment it is born
Its postings are stored uncompressed and cost memory
Its rows carry no ACL fields until the swap completes

questions.topic: Freshness SLAs and Lag Metrics for Ingestion and Index Builds
questions.question: How should a rebuild avoid staleness at publish?
options: Pause every ingestion path until the build completes
Publish half-built indexes hourly so freshness never lags
Snapshot at a recorded time, then replay before the swap
Run the build on larger machines so it finishes in an hour

questions.topic: Freshness SLAs and Lag Metrics for Ingestion and Index Builds
questions.question: A revocation at 09:10 takes effect at 09:32 against a 5-minute SLA because compaction locked the segment. What is the correct follow-up?
options: Relax the revocation SLA from five minutes to thirty minutes
Forbid compaction entirely on segments that serve live queries
Move the serving index onto larger and faster hardware
Couple compaction windows to SLA alerts and an error budget

questions.topic: Production Retrieval Metrics: Hit Rate, MRR, Reranker Scores
questions.question: What does the zero-hit rate measure?
options: The fraction of queries that returned nothing useful
The count of documents that still have no embeddings
The share of cache entries that never once served a hit
The number of days since the last full index build

questions.topic: Production Retrieval Metrics: Hit Rate, MRR, Reranker Scores
questions.question: What does production MRR compute from interaction logs?
options: The rank at which the newest document appears
The mean rank across every result that was returned
The reciprocal rank of the first clicked or cited result
The number of sessions recorded for each distinct query

questions.topic: Production Retrieval Metrics: Hit Rate, MRR, Reranker Scores
questions.question: The reranker top-1 score distribution shifts with no code change deployed. What does that indicate?
options: The reranker has begun to overfit its training set
The inputs changed: new query types or corpus growth
The serving accelerator pool is misconfigured for batch
The dashboards are stale and showing yesterday's data

questions.topic: Production Retrieval Metrics: Hit Rate, MRR, Reranker Scores
questions.question: Post-dedupe candidate counts suddenly halve. What do funnel attrition metrics provide?
options: A reason to switch deduplication off for the moment
Proof that the query mix has shifted with the season
Evidence that the golden set needs rebuilding first
An address for the stage whose output changed shape

questions.topic: Production Retrieval Metrics: Hit Rate, MRR, Reranker Scores
questions.question: What does a rising re-query rate usually mean?
options: Users are enjoying the process of refining searches
The corpus is growing and offering more to explore
First answers are failing, so users rephrase them
The answer cache TTL has been set far too long

questions.topic: Production Retrieval Metrics: Hit Rate, MRR, Reranker Scores
questions.question: After a chunker deploy, reranker top-1 p50 falls from 0.81 to 0.74 and post-dedupe candidates halve. What is the diagnosis?
options: The reranker model drifted between two published versions
The new chunker emits near-duplicates that dedupe collapses
BM25 lost its term dictionary during the same deploy
The golden set has rotted and no longer mirrors real traffic

questions.topic: Golden Query Sets and Regression Canaries for Index Changes
questions.question: What is a golden query set?
options: A versioned, class-stratified set of adjudicated queries
The most frequent production queries from last month
Every query the system served during the last quarter
The queries that currently earn the highest reranker scores

questions.topic: Golden Query Sets and Regression Canaries for Index Changes
questions.question: What is the correct acceptance rule for an index change?
options: The average metric across the set must improve overall
At least half of the individual queries must improve
No query class may regress beyond its own threshold
End-to-end latency must stay within ten percent of before

questions.topic: Golden Query Sets and Regression Canaries for Index Changes
questions.question: A planted document must rank first for `canary refund policy xq9` and is queried every minute. What does a miss detect?
options: Index corruption, an ACL regression, or a serving bug
Slow office networking between the prober and the API
Golden-set rot as the product's language moves on
A judge model that has begun preferring its own outputs

questions.topic: Golden Query Sets and Regression Canaries for Index Changes
questions.question: How does a freshness canary work?
options: A planted document is updated hourly and its lag measured
A judge model scores how fresh each generated answer sounds
The entire index is rebuilt hourly so the lag never grows
Logs are sampled for the newest write timestamps per stage

questions.topic: Golden Query Sets and Regression Canaries for Index Changes
questions.question: A team tunes BM25 parameters until the golden set passes. What is the safeguard?
options: Report the metrics with more decimal places of precision
Restrict parameter tuning to weekends and quiet periods
Add a second and third LLM judge to the scoring panel
Hold out a slice used only for validation, never tuning

questions.topic: Golden Query Sets and Regression Canaries for Index Changes
questions.question: What is the standard fix for golden-set rot?
options: Freeze the set permanently so results stay comparable
Quarterly review, plus every incident donating its queries
Double the size of the set automatically each quarter
Replace the adjudicated queries with synthetic ones

questions.topic: Diagnosing Quality Drops: Data Drift vs Index Defect vs Model Change
questions.question: A gradual, weeks-long decline concentrated in one query segment, with stable per-stage counts, points to which family?
options: Index defect
Model change
Data drift
Judge drift

questions.topic: Diagnosing Quality Drops: Data Drift vs Index Defect vs Model Change
questions.question: A sudden quality step change aligned with a build timestamp, with canaries firing, points to which family?
options: Index defect
Data drift
Seasonal traffic
Verbosity bias

questions.topic: Diagnosing Quality Drops: Data Drift vs Index Defect vs Model Change
questions.question: Metrics moved uniformly while user outcomes held still. What is the likely cause?
options: Index corruption introduced by the most recent build
A judge model update moved the metric, not the system
The corpus roughly doubled in size over one weekend
The reranker began timing out under concurrent load

questions.topic: Diagnosing Quality Drops: Data Drift vs Index Defect vs Model Change
questions.question: What is the first question in the diagnostic order, and why?
options: Which model is largest, because size decides quality
Who deployed last, because ownership resolves disputes
When did it start, because a timestamp match convicts
How many users complained, because volume ranks severity

questions.topic: Diagnosing Quality Drops: Data Drift vs Index Defect vs Model Change
questions.question: The golden set reproduces the quality drop offline. What does that eliminate?
options: Every possible model change, since those models run offline too
Live-only causes such as cache state, ACLs, and traffic mix
Any form of data drift, which needs live traffic to appear
The need for production canaries on the serving index

questions.topic: Diagnosing Quality Drops: Data Drift vs Index Defect vs Model Change
questions.question: How should every quality-drop diagnosis end?
options: By scheduling a full rewrite of the affected pipeline
By lowering every alert threshold to catch more events
By archiving the incident notes in the team's wiki
By adding the metric or canary that would have caught it
